title: Derived structure unit and its ordinary and fibre comparisons
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact separated flat morphism of schemes [def-pc-morphism-conventions], with flatness as in [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Put $J=\mathcal O_S[0]$ and $E=Rf_*\mathcal O_X[0]$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image] in the derived category [def-pc-derived-category]. There exist $a:J\to E$ and isomorphisms $e_0:H^0(J)\cong\mathcal O_S$, $e_1:H^0(E)\cong f_*\mathcal O_X$, such that $H^0(a)e_1=e_0f^\sharp$, where $f^\sharp$ denotes the ordinary module structure map. At every $s\in S$ the negative cohomology of $Li_s^*E$ [def-pc-derived-pullback] is zero. If the canonical map $\kappa(s)\to H^0(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})$ [def-pc-base-change] is an isomorphism, then $H^0(Li_s^*a)$ is an isomorphism. No conclusion about surjectivity of $f^\sharp_s$ is part of this statement.

proof.text: Compute [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image] on $\mathcal O_X[0]$ by a nonnegative injective resolution. Compose the single-complex ordinary structure map with the resolution augmentation and localize to obtain $a$. The source single-complex cohomology is $\mathcal O_S$. Direct image is left exact; hence the resolution augmentation identifies $H^0(E)$ with $f_*\mathcal O_X$, and its naturality gives the equation for $a$ and $e_0,e_1$.

The structure sheaf is relatively flat because $f$ is flat. Apply [lem-pc-relatively-flat-canonical-module-base-change] to the residue-field fibre square. Use [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf] to identify the pulled-back structure sheaf with that on the fibre. Naturality of the canonical base-change mate identifies the pulled-back $a$ with the fibre structure map. A derived direct image of a sheaf has no negative cohomology. On the affine spectrum of a field, global sections detect isomorphisms of quasi-coherent modules. Thus the assumed isomorphism on fibre global functions implies that $H^0(Li_s^*a)$ is invertible.

theorem exists_flat_derived_structure_unit
    [∀ Y : Scheme.{u},
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f] [Flat f] :
    let O := SheafOfModules.unit S.ringCatSheaf
    let J := (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings S.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj O
    let E := (schemeDerivedDirectImage f).obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj
        (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf))
    let H := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings S.toRingedSpace)) 0
    ∃ (a : J ⟶ E) (e₀ : H.obj J ≅ O)
      (e₁ : H.obj E ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj
        (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)),
      H.map a ≫ e₁.hom = e₀.hom ≫
        SheafOfModules.unitToPushforwardObjUnit f.toRingCatSheafHom ∧
      (∀ (s : S) (i : ℤ), i < 0 → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (Spec (S.residueField s)).toRingedSpace)) i).obj
          ((derivedPullback (S.fromSpecResidueField s)).obj E))) ∧
      (∀ s : S, IsIso (f.fiberToSpecResidueField s).appTop →
        IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (Spec (S.residueField s)).toRingedSpace)) 0).map
            ((derivedPullback (S.fromSpecResidueField s)).map a)))
